questionText: What does XSL do for an XML document?
options: It transforms and renders it, as CSS styles HTML
It checks that every tag is properly nested
It declares the entities used in the document
It encodes the characters into binary form
correctAnswer: It transforms and renders it, as CSS styles HTML
explanation: XSL is a style sheet for XML, as CSS is for HTML; it transforms and renders the XML document, as seen in the XSL Output view. Encoding characters into binary is set by the encoding in the XML declaration.

questionText: How many root elements can an XML document have?
explanation: An XML document can have only one root element, which is the parent of all other elements, such as <people> in the athletes example.

questionText: What does DTD stand for in XML?
explanation: A Document Type Definition (DTD) defines the structure and the legal elements of an XML document, and an application can use it to check that XML data is valid.

questionText: Which is the correct syntax for a comment in XML?
explanation: The syntax for a comment in XML is <!-- This is a comment -->, the same as in HTML; the XML parser ignores comments. The // and /* */ forms are comments in programming languages, not markup.

questionText: How many pre-defined entity references are there in XML?
explanation: There are 5 pre-defined entity references in XML: < (<), > (>), & (&), ' (') and " (").

questionText: What does PCDATA stand for in a DTD such as <!ELEMENT first (#PCDATA)>?
explanation: PCDATA stands for Parsed Character Data, the text found between the start tag and end tag of an XML element, such as Abebech.

questionText: Which top-level domain extension is meant for non-profit organizations?
explanation: Common domain extensions include .com for commercial sites, .edu for educational institutions, .gov for government, .org for non-profit organizations, .mil for military and .net for network.

questionText: Which XML Notepad view shows an XML document after it has been transformed by a style sheet?
explanation: XML Notepad shows a document in Tree View, which displays its structure, and XSL Output, which shows it transformed by an XSL style sheet. Page Source is the browser option for viewing raw code.

questionText: Which file does a web server return by default when a site's address is typed without a file name?
explanation: index.html contains the main home page, and web servers are set by default to return it when no file name is given, so moe.gov.et returns moe.gov.et/index.html. CSS and JS files hold styles and scripts.

questionText: Which website folder holds the code that adds interactive functionality, such as buttons that load data when clicked?
explanation: The scripts folder contains all the JavaScript code used to add interactive functionality to the site. The CSS folder holds the code used to style the site.

questionText: What is the main purpose of XML?
options: Displaying data in a formatted layout
Styling web pages with colors and fonts
Adding interactive buttons to web pages
explanation: XML is designed to store data and is popularly used for the transfer of data; it describes structure, not presentation. Displaying formatted data is the purpose of HTML.

questionText: How do the tags used in XML differ from the tags used in HTML?
options: XML tags are defined by the author to fit the document
XML tags are fixed and listed in a standard catalogue
XML uses the same predefined tags as HTML but in capitals
XML tags may only be used inside the HTML body section
correctAnswer: XML tags are defined by the author to fit the document
explanation: HTML uses predefined tags such as <head> and <title>, whereas in XML you define your own custom tags that meet the exact needs of your document, which makes data easier to organize and search.

questionText: Why is <name>Ibrahim</Name> an error in XML?
options: Element names are case sensitive, so the tags do not match
Element names cannot start with a lowercase letter
Text inside an element must be in quotation marks
An element name must contain at least one digit
correctAnswer: Element names are case sensitive, so the tags do not match
explanation: XML elements are case sensitive, so the end tag must match the start tag exactly; <name> and </Name> are different names. Lowercase names are allowed, and element text needs no quotation marks.

questionText: Which XML fragment is properly nested?
explanation: XML elements must not overlap and must be properly nested: an element opened inside another must close before its parent closes, as in <Student><Name>Almaz</Name></Student>.

questionText: Which element name breaks the XML naming rules?
explanation: Element names must start with a letter or underscore, so <1dollar> is not allowed. Names can contain letters, digits, hyphens, underscores and periods, so the others are valid.

questionText: How does XML treat several spaces typed in a row inside an element, compared with HTML?
options: XML keeps all the spaces, while HTML reduces them to one
XML reduces them to one space, while HTML keeps all of them
Both XML and HTML keep every space exactly as typed
Both XML and HTML reduce the spaces to a single space
correctAnswer: XML keeps all the spaces, while HTML reduces them to one
explanation: XML does not truncate multiple white-spaces, while in HTML multiple white-spaces are truncated to a single white-space.

questionText: Which part at the start of an XML document gives the version and the character encoding, such as UTF-8?
explanation: The XML declaration (processing instruction), such as <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>, describes the document's general characteristics including its version and encoding. The root element encloses all the content.

questionText: After <!ENTITY publisher "Berhanena Selam Printing"> is declared, what does the parser do when it meets &publisher; in the document?
options: It replaces it with the declared text
It shows the text &publisher; unchanged on screen
It reports an error because & is illegal
It creates a new element named publisher
correctAnswer: It replaces it with the declared text
explanation: When the parser meets an ampersand and semicolon identifying an entity reference, it looks up the name in the entity declarations and replaces &publisher; with the content it represents, Berhanena Selam Printing.

questionText: Why does opening an XML file in a browser not produce a nicely formatted page?
options: XML only holds content; a style sheet must present it
Browsers cannot read XML files and always show an error message
XML files must first be converted into a relational database
The XML declaration hides all of the content from the browser
correctAnswer: XML only holds content; a style sheet must present it
explanation: XML is just information wrapped in tags; it is meant to hold content so that when combined with resources such as a style sheet (XSL) it becomes a finished product. Browsers do show it, usually as color-coded elements.

questionText: Which is listed as a disadvantage of XML?
options: It has no intrinsic data type support
It separates the data from HTML
It makes documents transportable across systems
It simplifies the platform exchange process
correctAnswer: It has no intrinsic data type support
explanation: Disadvantages of XML include needing a processing application, confusing and redundant syntax, and no intrinsic data type support. Separating data from HTML and making documents transportable are advantages.

questionText: Where does the domain name appear in a web address such as http://www.example.gov.et/?
explanation: A domain name is the part of the internet address that comes after www; in http://www.moe.gov.et/ the domain name is moe.gov. The part after the last slash would be a page or file name.

questionText: What must a website have to enable HTTPS?
explanation: To enable HTTPS, a website needs an SSL (Secure Sockets Layer) certificate, which encrypts information sent between visitors and the site. A domain extension has nothing to do with security.

questionText: In the Bookstore example, which elements have element content rather than text content?
explanation: <Bookstore> and <Book> have element contents because they contain other elements, while <title>, <author>, <year> and <price> have text content such as Kebede Michael.

questionText: How should an attribute be written when its value itself contains double quotation marks?
options: Enclose the value in single quotation marks
Leave the value without any quotation marks
Enclose the value in double quotation marks twice
Move the value into a comment beside the element
correctAnswer: Enclose the value in single quotation marks
explanation: Attribute values must always be quoted with single or double quotes; if the value contains double quotation marks, single quotation marks are used, as in name='Tilahun Gessesse "Kome Limerkish"'.

questionText: Which characters are strictly illegal inside XML element content?
explanation: Only the characters < and & are strictly illegal in XML; the greater-than character is legal, although it is a good habit to replace it with >.

questionText: <person gender="female"> and a <gender>female</gender> child element inside <person> are two ways to store gender. Which statement about them is correct?
options: Both give the same information and there is no rule about which to use
Only the attribute form is valid, because elements cannot hold such data
Only the element form is valid, because attributes cannot hold text
The attribute form must be declared with an ENTITY first
correctAnswer: Both give the same information and there is no rule about which to use
explanation: In one example gender is an attribute and in the other an element; both provide the same information, and there are no rules about when to use attributes or elements in XML.

questionText: Which comparison of XML and HTML is correct?
options: XML is content driven, while HTML is format driven
XML ignores small coding errors, while HTML allows none
XML is case insensitive, while HTML is case sensitive
XML closing tags are optional, while HTML needs them
correctAnswer: XML is content driven, while HTML is format driven
explanation: XML is content driven and HTML is format driven. The other statements are reversed: XML allows no coding errors, is case sensitive and requires closing tags, while HTML ignores small errors and does not always need them.

questionText: What is web hosting?
options: Providing web server space where websites are stored
Registering a unique domain name for an organization
Encrypting visitors' data with an SSL certificate
Designing the folders and pages of a website
correctAnswer: Providing web server space where websites are stored
explanation: Hosting companies provide web hosting services, meaning online space for storing websites on a web server, where the website actually resides. Registering a domain name is a separate step of publishing.

questionText: What does <!DOCTYPE album [...]> define in a DTD?
options: The root element of the document
The character encoding of the file
A comment ignored by the parser
correctAnswer: The root element of the document
explanation: In a DTD, !DOCTYPE album defines the root element of the document, album, while !ELEMENT lines define each element. The encoding is given in the XML declaration.

questionText: Which statement about an empty XML element is correct?
options: It can be written as <element></element> or <element />
It must contain at least one attribute to be valid
It can only be written as <element> with no end tag
It must hold the word EMPTY between its two tags
correctAnswer: It can be written as <element></element> or <element />
explanation: An element without content is an empty element, and it can be written either as <element></element> or as <element />. A start tag without an end tag is not allowed in well-formed XML.
